overallVerdict.headline: The 0-High result is HONEST and independently confirmed on structural grounds. The 0-Medium result is an UNDER-CALL. Two findings must be raised to Medium: L-01 (setRewardToken bricks the sole permissionless entry point) and L-02 (documented sink retirement permanently destroys the streamer buffer). In both cases the classifier applied a test that C4 Medium does not contain — 'the owner can cure it' for L-01, and 'the escalating assumption is unevidenced' for L-02 — and in the L-02 case the assumption is in fact EVIDENCED in the project's own migration scripts, which the classifier explicitly flagged as the one question it could not resolve from source. I resolved it.
overallVerdict.law1Note: Per the symmetry rule, a defensible-either-way call is kept HIGHER, not lower. Neither raise here relies on that tiebreak: both are affirmatively justified on evidence. The classifier repeatedly used the conservative-when-uncertain rule in the WRONG DIRECTION — it says classify conservatively, which for a self-audit protecting user funds means keeping the higher severity and flagging, not lowering the severity and attaching a reopen trigger.

pattern1_ownerCurableReflex.observation: Five of the nine findings are downgraded, in whole or in part, on the reasoning 'the actor who causes it is the actor who cures it' (L-01, F-01) or 'the condition is reversible by the same call that caused it' (L-04, L-02). This is applied as a general demotion rule.
pattern1_ownerCurableReflex.ruling: INVALID AS A SEVERITY RULE. C4 Medium is 'assets are not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted'. There is no recoverability carve-out in that criterion. Recoverability bears on DURATION of impact, not on WHETHER availability was impacted. Curability is a mitigating factor to be stated, not a criterion that defeats the Medium bar.
pattern1_ownerCurableReflex.law3Ruling: CLAUDE.md Law 3 is explicit that a non-obvious owner footgun is in scope 'at honest severity' and is 'surfaced as an operational hazard'. 'At honest severity' exists precisely to block the automatic demotion the classifier performed. The correct severity of an operational hazard is the severity of the impact it unlocks.

pattern2_internalInconsistency.observation: The stable-yield-accumulator LEDGER already ranks M-01 at MEDIUM: 'Unconfigured non-18-decimal token treated as 18-dec 1:1 (fail-open default) — one forgotten setter'. That is an owner-omission footgun, owner-curable with a single call on SYA itself, ranked Medium and status acknowledged.
pattern2_internalInconsistency.ruling: Run-14 L-01 is a STRICTLY WORSE footgun than ledger M-01 on every axis: the triggering action is documented as SAFE (M-01's is merely omitted), the outage is total rather than partial, and the cure requires two ordered calls on two OTHER contracts rather than one call on SYA. Ranking L-01 below ledger M-01 is not defensible as a consistent application of the same criteria to the same project.
pattern2_internalInconsistency.corpusPrecedent: The wider audit corpus consistently ranks owner-triggered bricks at Medium — stable-staker ss10m1 (phantom-staker brick, Medium), phlimbo-ea V3-M-04 (relocated brick, Medium), phstaging YS-21 (live-staker-pause, Medium). Run-14 is the outlier, not the corpus.

pattern3_reopenTriggerAsSeveritySubstitu.observation: Four findings carry 'REOPEN AT MEDIUM if X' triggers where X is a deployment-time or ops fact.
pattern3_reopenTriggerAsSeveritySubstitu.ruling: The triggers are excellent practice and must be preserved. But a reopen trigger is a DETECTION mechanism, not a severity discount. Two of them (L-01/F-01 shared-ownership, L-02 sink-retirement) are conditions that will be decided by ops with no guarantee an audit re-runs at that moment. Where the condition is undecided (L-01) or affirmatively evidenced (L-02), the trigger must accompany the higher severity, not substitute for it.

findings.title: setRewardToken is an undocumented re-arm trigger that bricks claim()

analysis.assetRisk: NONE. Concur fully. No theft, no direct loss. Correctly rules out High.
analysis.availabilityImpact: TOTAL and PERMANENT-UNTIL-CURED outage of claim() — the only permissionless entry point and the sole mechanism converting yield-strategy surplus into phlimbo rewards. This is the C4 Medium criterion stated almost verbatim: 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted.' The classifier's own availabilityImpact field concedes exactly this, then declines to rank it accordingly.
analysis.attackPath: VALID — no hypotheticals. Not an attacker path but a fully constructive one-call state transition from a correctly-configured working system to a bricked one. Verified independently at f704130: setRewardToken (src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:417-420) is a bare assignment with only a zero-address check, no rail guard, no event; claim() (:594-601) hard-requires a registered (nudge, rewardToken) stream inside the nudgeAmount > 0 branch with no try/catch.
analysis.conditions: nudgeSplit > 0 (the live-donation branch — i.e. the production configuration). No external, attacker-uncontrolled precondition. Rule 4 does not apply.
analysis.impact: PoC-grade, exceeds the C4 PoC bar. Exact revert selector 0xd62cbfe8 (NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered) against the REAL NudgeStreamer @5015f1b, with direct storage assertions that the old (sink, oldReward) stream survives at duration == DURATION while (sink, newReward) is duration == 0, plus a 365-day warp confirming permanence and a positive control gating the whole suite.

findings.disagreementReason: Two independent defects in the downgrade rationale. (1) The stated rationale is 'the actor who causes the outage is the actor who cures it, with one key, in bounded time'. C4 Medium contains no such test — recoverability bounds the duration of an availability impact, it does not negate it. (2) The factual premise is weaker than presented. SWING-001 resolves shared ownership as CONVENTION (a preflight require in one staging script, plus one Ledger key used 94x), and the classifier's own statedAssumptionAndResidualRisk concedes that NudgeStreamer and BatchNFTMinterMultiToken are NOT YET DEPLOYED and take a free constructor initialOwner with 'NO code-level enforcement'. So the Medium-defeating fact is an inference about a deployment that has not happened. Under the symmetry rule an undecided swing factor is resolved to the HIGHER severity and flagged, which is also what the classification brief instructed ('an unresolvable ownership question be classified on the more conservative (Medium) reading') — the classifier declared it resolved on inferential evidence and thereby escaped an instruction that was written for exactly this case. Note also that the Tier-3 document itself states at line 102-103: 'this remediation requires the streamer owner and the batch-minter owner, not the SYA owner who caused the outage.'
aggravatorsThatSurviveAndCompound: NON-OBVIOUSNESS IS MAXIMAL: the contract's own ops NatSpec (:69-79) asserts a CLOSED enumeration — 'there are three failure modes' — and names only setNudgeAddress as a re-arm trigger. An owner who reads the runbook correctly and follows it exactly still bricks the rail. This is not a missing warning; it is an affirmative representation that the action is safe. Law 3's surprise test is met decisively.

SILENT: the only load-bearing address setter in the contract with no event. Eight siblings emit. Off-chain monitoring cannot observe the state change; detection depends on someone noticing reverts on a permissionless function with no guaranteed call cadence.

ORDERED CROSS-CONTRACT CURE: repair is setNudgeTokenWhitelist then registerStream on two other contracts, and reversing the order reverts NudgeStreamer__NotWhitelisted (0x0dc85695) — a second trap inside the remedy.
findings.notes: Raise to Medium. Every escalation trigger, the constructive proof, the law3Ruling and the recommendation carry over UNCHANGED — the classifier's analysis is excellent and its evidence is what convicts its own conclusion. Only the label is wrong. The setNudgeSplit(0) escape does not rescue the Low: it restores liveness by disabling 100% of the nudge routing, i.e. it trades the availability impact for a total functional one.
downstreamCorrections: Re-rank as M-01 for run-14 (ledger continuation label to be assigned by finding-manager; ledger M-01 is taken).
Requires a coded PoC per C4 Medium rules — already satisfied by test/NudgeStreamerLiveness_SYA.t.sol test_P1_B; pocRequired must flip from false to true and pocStatus is already sufficient.
Route to an individual finding write-up, NOT the QA report body.

findings.title: Documented nudge migration orphans the old pair's streamer buffer

analysis.assetRisk: PERMANENT, UNRESCUABLE LOSS of up to one full standing float (donationRate x duration; ~30 days of nudge donations, ~$60k at the run's illustrative parameters) once the old sink is retired. Not dust, and not recoverable by any party.
analysis.attackPath: VALID. No attacker. Owner performs the DOCUMENTED migration; the runbook (:82-90) prescribes registering the NEW pair first and contains no drain step for the OLD one.
analysis.conditions: The old sink stops flushing. RESOLVED AS THE DEFAULT CASE, not an exception — see resolvedSwingFactor below.
analysis.impact: C4 Medium: 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'. Both the assumption and the external requirement are now documented and evidenced.

findings.disagreementReason: The classifier flagged this itself as the single item most likely to be re-ranked upward and stated the exact deciding question: 'Is decommissioning the old sink the EXPECTED outcome of a nudge migration in this protocol's ops practice? If yes ... this becomes a Medium value leak.' It then declined to answer, recording 'an assumption not evidenced at f704130'. That is a scope error, not a genuine unknown: the evidence is not in the SYA source, it is in the sibling staging repo the classifier already mined for SWING-001. I searched it. The answer is YES.

resolvedSwingFactor.question: Is retiring the old nudge sink the expected outcome of a sink migration?
resolvedSwingFactor.verdict: YES — retirement is the project's documented, scripted, and repeatedly-executed ops practice.
evidence: lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/script/ReplaceBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:6 — the script's own header states its purpose is to '...retire the old exploited contract'; step 7 at :33 and :482-492 is titled 'Retire old contract'.

lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/script/MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:10,:54,:496-510 — an independent second migration script with the identical step 8 'Retire old contract', commented 'zero the old nudge config so it can never pay out again.'

Both _retireOld() implementations neutralize the old sink's nudge configuration: setNudgePaymentToken(address(0)) and setNudgeSize(0). Retirement is therefore not incidental — permanent neutralization is the stated intent.

CRITICAL: both retirement routines gate on `require(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0, "old contract still holds USDC")`. This drain assertion reads the SINK's balance and is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to the NudgeStreamer buffer keyed to that sink. Post-story-026 the value no longer sits where the safety check looks. The documented retirement procedure would PASS ITS OWN SAFETY GATE while permanently destroying up to donationRate x duration.
resolvedSwingFactor.caveat: The two retirement scripts target the V1 IOldBatchMinter surface (setNudgePaymentToken/setNudgeSize), predating BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, so they will not literally execute against the new sink. They are evidence of ops PRACTICE and INTENT, which is precisely what the classifier's question asked for. This caveat lowers confidence from 'certain' to 'high'; it does not change the verdict.

whyTheLowRationaleFails.classifierClaim: 'BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint is PERMISSIONLESS and its step-3.5 flush loop runs UNCONDITIONALLY, so ANY caller can drain the orphan indefinitely.'
whyTheLowRationaleFails.ruling: TRUE ONLY WHILE THE OLD SINK REMAINS OPERATIONAL — which retirement is specifically designed to end. I verified three independent severing mechanisms on the retirement path, ANY ONE of which is sufficient: (1) batchMint is `whenNotPaused` (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:461-465) and pause() exists at :358 — a paused retired sink cannot flush at all; (2) the flush loop iterates `_nudgeTokens` (:525-532), and setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token,false) at :315 removes the token via swap-and-pop — this is the direct MultiToken analogue of the retirement scripts' setNudgePaymentToken(0), and it is the same mechanism the classifier itself documents as L-04; (3) setNudgeStreamer(address(0)) at :290 short-circuits the entire flush block. The permissionless-flush escape hatch is available exactly until someone performs the routine operation that creates the problem.
whyTheLowRationaleFails.unrescuability: Independently verified: NudgeStreamer's complete external surface is registerStream, collectNudge, pullPendingStream, pendingStream, plus Ownable — there is no rescue, sweep or withdraw, and no fallback (Tier-3 test_P2_D probed ten signatures, all revert). pullPendingStream is msg.sender-keyed, so ONLY the retired sink can pull its own buffer. registerStream merely re-spreads the same buffer to the SAME recipient. Note the asymmetry that makes this Medium rather than Low: value already SETTLED into the sink is recoverable by the owner via rescueERC20 (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:383), but value still held in the STREAMER buffer has no rescue path from any address.

findings.notes: Raise to Medium as a value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements. This is a distinct impact from L-01 and does not double-count it: different trigger (setNudgeAddress + retirement vs setRewardToken), different impact class (value destruction vs availability), different fix. The recommendation the classifier already wrote is correct and becomes more urgent: add a step 0 to the ops runbook draining the old (sink, token) stream before repointing and asserting pendingStream(old, token) == 0, and extend the retirement scripts' `require(balanceOf(OLD) == 0)` gate to cover the streamer buffer — that assertion is currently a false assurance.
downstreamCorrections: Re-rank as run-14 M-02; requires a coded PoC per C4 Medium rules — one does not yet exist and should be commissioned (extend NudgeStreamerLiveness_SYA.t.sol: fund a buffer, repoint, de-whitelist/pause the old sink, then assert no address can recover it).
Preserve the flaggedForHumanReview entry but restate it as ANSWERED, with the ops question converted into a confirmation request rather than an open swing factor.

findings.title: story-026 makes an external post-deploy-ZERO contract a hard precondition of the only permissionless entry point
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED (Low) — but the stated reasoning is partly invalid and must be replaced

analysis.attackPath: Valid, no hypotheticals, but its DISTINCT manifestation is genuinely weaker than L-01's.
analysis.impact: Availability, but at t=0 before the rail carries value, with a unilateral SYA-only escape (setNudgeSplit(0), test_P1_F).

reasoningCorrection.invalidArgument: The doubleCountingNote — 'Ranking this design item at Medium as well would count the same availability impact twice and dilute the report' — is NOT a valid severity argument and must be struck. Severity is a property of a finding's own impact; report economy is a dedup/presentation question. If two findings genuinely share one impact they should be MERGED, not both discounted. Left standing, this reasoning is exactly the failure mode the task asked me to test: a Medium-shaped impact escaping by being split across two Lows.
reasoningCorrection.validArgumentThatSustainsLow: F-01 nonetheless holds at Low on its OWN merits, for reasons the classifier also gave and which do not depend on double-counting: (a) the exposure is the POST-DEPLOY DEFAULT, so it binds before the rail has ever carried value — there is nothing to lose and nothing to interrupt; (b) it is unilaterally escapable from the SYA key alone via setNudgeSplit(0), with no dependence on the shared-ownership inference that L-01's downgrade rested on; (c) the failure is loud and pre-transactional, so it cannot silently degrade. An unarmed rail that has never been armed is a deployment checklist item, not an availability incident.
reasoningCorrection.netEffect: Once L-01 is raised to Medium, the double-counting concern is moot in both directions — the Medium-shaped manifestation is ranked at Medium where it belongs, and the design item sits at Low where its own impact places it. The two are correctly separated rather than jointly suppressed.

findings.notes: Keep at Low, keep the spec-conformance routing (Law 2), keep the escalation triggers. Replace the doubleCountingNote with the standalone rationale above so the Low does not rest on an argument that would let impact leak between findings. The Law-1-over-Law-2 adjudication is correct and well made: a faithful implementation of an unsafe story is escalated, not blessed.

findings.title: Unrescuable standing float converging to donationRate x duration
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED (Low), with one escalation trigger reclassified from exceptional to EVIDENCED

analysis.assetRisk: The float itself is NOT a loss. Independently verified: the sink receives continuously at rate r, and in steady state receives the full donation rate — the standing B* is work-in-progress, not leakage. test_P2_D confirms registerStream re-spreads the same buffer to the same recipient with the owner's balance unchanged, and that shrinking duration accelerates delivery TO the sink, draining the streamer to zero. 'Permanently in transit to the intended recipient' is an accurate framing, not a euphemism. It holds.
analysis.attackPath: None — normal operation. The griefer amplification is correctly capped: strictly negative-EV, no competitor excluded, no value redirected.
analysis.conditions: Loss requires an exceptional realisation trigger.
analysis.impact: Low, correctly assigned for the right reason (exceptional trigger) and explicitly NOT because the amount is dust.

findings.valuationRulingCheck: CONCUR. The econ-scanner's REAL-LOSS-if-realised ruling is correct and correctly preserved verbatim. The nudge share is claimer-paid CONSIDERATION entering the protocol, not Tokemak-style yield on protocol-owned capital, so the standing memory rule externally-derived-yield-opportunity-cost-not-loss is properly ruled INAPPLICABLE to this leg. The classifier checked the right rule and reached the right answer rather than reaching for it as a suppression.
findings.correctionRequired: Trigger (b) 'the sink is retired and never flushes again' is listed alongside blacklist and claims-ceasing as equally exceptional. Per SWING-003 above, sink retirement is the project's DOCUMENTED AND SCRIPTED ops practice, not an exception. That trigger must be reclassified as EVIDENCED.
findings.whyStillLowRatherThanRaised: The realisation of that now-evidenced trigger is ranked at L-02 (raised to Medium), where the actionable SYA-side fix lives. L-03 is the steady-state property whose root cause (NudgeStreamer.sol:150-153 full-duration rate recompute) is OUT OF SCOPE and correctly parked as PARK-001. Raising BOTH would be genuine double counting of one pool of value. Correct split: L-02 Medium carries the loss; L-03 Low carries the magnitude, the r x D scaling law and the custody dead-end that give L-02 its size. This is the one place in the run where an anti-double-counting argument IS legitimate, because the two findings would be ranking the same dollars.
findings.notes: Confirmed Low. Keep the $60k magnitude and the r x D scaling law on the record — they now quantify L-02's Medium. The Tier-3 in-transit nuance must continue to be carried verbatim into any write-up; it is the reason this is not over-severed.

findings.title: Nudge-token whitelist is registration-time-only; collectNudge never re-checks it

analysis.assetRisk: None while the sink is live. Verified independently: setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token,true) at BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:315 re-adds the token to _nudgeTokens, restoring both the step-3.5 pullPendingStream loop (:525-532) and distribution of the settled balance; the stream registration on NudgeStreamer is never revoked. Value is paused, not leaked. Additionally rescueERC20 (:383) covers anything already settled into the sink.
analysis.conditions: The de-whitelisted token is SYA's live rewardToken while donations flow.

findings.notes: Low is correct. The residualAggravator the classifier kept is the right one and must survive into the report: SYA emits nothing and reverts nothing, so DETECTION is the weak link, not recovery. Two cross-references to add: (1) the permanent variant of this condition — de-whitelist as part of retirement — is now covered at Medium by L-02, so this entry should point there rather than reading as fully benign; (2) this is the same severing mechanism L-02's Low rationale depended on being unavailable, which is the internal tension that raising L-02 resolves.
findings.reasoningCaveat: The downgrade cites SHARED ownership as weakening the 'third-party owner has no visibility' aggravator. That leans on the same inferential, undeployed-contract premise as L-01. It does not change the outcome here — L-04 is Low on reversibility alone, independent of who holds the keys — but the ownership clause should be dropped from the rationale so the Low does not inherit a premise it does not need.

findings.title: Standing phlimbo allowance never revoked on setPhlimbo or setRewardToken repoint

analysis.assetRisk: Genuinely thin. Verified: setPhlimbo (:405-411) and setRewardToken (:417-420) both repoint without touching the allowance, but SYA holds ~zero rewardToken between claims and claim() is nonReentrant, so a stale grantee has no meaningful balance to reach.
analysis.attackPath: State hygiene, not an exploit path — correctly characterised under the non-malicious-owner assumption.
analysis.impact: Minimal in isolation; real as L-01's second blast leg.

findings.knownInvalidCheck: CONCUR with the rejection of the C4 approve-race exclusion. This is a standing allowance OUTLIVING its grantee across a repoint — a different defect from ERC-20 approve front-running. Correctly reasoned, not hand-waved.
findings.notes: Low is correct and is not under-called: no attacker under Law 3, and no window. The distinctFromLedgerL02 cross-reference is important and well argued — over-persistence vs under-supply are opposite failure modes of the same variable and must not be merged. Keep the qa-bundler adjacency instruction.

findings.title: NudgeStreamer throttles arrival rate, not capture size; SYA NatSpec :62 restates the over-claim
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED — the most disciplined item in the set

analysis.assetRisk: None to SYA. No principal lost, no treasury loss. The loss is to INTENT (proportionate distribution).
analysis.attackPath: The mechanism working as coded. Structurally correct: streaming converts instantaneous winner-take-all capture into DELAYED winner-take-all capture of the same total; it does not divide the pot. The t* = n*p/r result is parameter-independent.
analysis.conditions: Root cause lives entirely in an out-of-scope nested dependency.
analysis.impact: The only in-scope, first-party, actionable leg is a one-sentence documentary softening.

findings.oosRulingCheck: CONCUR IN FULL, and note it as exemplary Law-1 practice: the C4 OOS-root-cause exclusion is correctly treated as a PARTIAL match and used to set severity rather than to delete the finding, preserving the actionable first-party leg. Suppressing the whole item would have been a recall loss.
findings.notes: Low is correct and honestly reasoned — held at Low BECAUSE the root cause is OOS and SYA's own first-party text makes only the weaker, true timing claim. The mandatoryReportingCounterweight (must appear alongside POS-001, since story-026's narrow goal of killing the same-block claimer self-rebate IS genuinely achieved) is a fairness requirement and must survive to the report. Cross-repo routing is correct: EVIDENCE bearing on 858e9e80's residual, do NOT reopen that wont-fix from here, do NOT collapse with run-22 M-01.

findings.title: In-source NatSpec self-certifies the exposure as 'not an audit finding' with no backing artefact
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED (Low) — the single mild over-rank candidate in the set; no change recommended

analysis.conditions: None — the artefact is present in shipped source.
analysis.impact: Indirect: on audit assurance, not on the protocol.

findings.overstatementCheck: Asked adversarially, this is the one item that could be argued down to QA: nothing in it touches code, value or availability, and 'issues with comments' is the QA bucket by name. I am NOT recommending the lowering. The Low is sustained on the classifier's stronger ground: this is not passive documentation drift but an ACTIVE suppression attempt embedded in the artefact under audit, and it was load-bearing THIS RUN — honouring it would have removed L-01 and F-01 at sanitization. That is above the informational/style floor. The gap between Low and QA is also immaterial to disposition, since both route away from H/M.
findings.circularityRulingCheck: CONCUR UNCONDITIONALLY. Suppressing this finding on the strength of the sentence it indicts would let the code under audit adjudicate a finding against itself. The classifier also correctly applied NO severity discount and NO confidence reduction elsewhere on the strength of that comment. This is the correct handling and the strongest single judgement call in the run.
findings.notes: Keep at Low, keep the spec-conformance routing. The downstream instruction is correct and important: if the owner accepts the mandatory-streamer exposure it must be a real /ledger triage decision, and 'accepted, will fix' maps to fix-pending, NEVER acknowledged.

findings.title: Interface and dead-code hygiene
findings.notes: QA is correct. The borderline ruling against the C4 'unused view functions (QA at best)' and tool-noise rules is sound — that rule PLACES such items at QA rather than excluding them, so routing here satisfies it. Keep the unreachable decimals>18 instance regardless of trimming: it is load-bearing evidence for the SLITHER-001 false-positive drop. No asset, availability or function impact; no upgrade case exists.

whyNoHighOrMediumAudit.noHighRuling: CONFIRMED — and it is STRONGER than the classifier claimed.

fuzzDependencyAssessment.question: Does anything load-bearing rest on Tier-3 Property 3, which is a fuzz result (absence of evidence)?
fuzzDependencyAssessment.answer: NO. The classifier's honestyCaveat states Property 3 IS load-bearing for the noHigh ruling and should be handed to the symbolic-analyzer. That caveat is commendably honest but over-humble, and I can discharge it by inspection rather than by symbolic execution.
fuzzDependencyAssessment.reasoning: Property 3's operative claims are STRUCTURAL and readable directly from source at f704130, which I verified independently: in claim() (src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:582-605) both the nudge leg (:596-600) and the phlimbo leg (:601-603) sit strictly DOWNSTREAM of `IERC20(rewardToken).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), actualPayment)` (:583), and NEITHER is wrapped in try/catch — the NatSpec at :71 states 'there is no try/catch envelope here' and the code confirms it. Solidity's revert semantics then make atomicity a language guarantee, not an empirical observation: any leg revert unwinds the payment, the skimmed surplus and the NFT burn together. A claimer cannot retain skimmed surplus while suppressing a leg. claim() is additionally nonReentrant.
fuzzDependencyAssessment.conclusion: The 128,000 Foundry calls and the 50,000-sequence Medusa campaign CORROBORATE a structurally-guaranteed property; they do not carry it. The noHigh ruling therefore does not rest on absence of evidence and does not need a Halmos PASS to stand. The honesty caveat should be RETAINED in the report (it is good practice and correctly scopes the six structural invariants, which DO rest on fuzz) but amended to record that the specific atomicity property underpinning noHigh is discharged structurally.
fuzzDependencyAssessment.residualUnknown: The fuzz-only results that remain genuinely unproven are the six structural invariants (globalConservation, splitConservation, noResidual, registrySync, nftCostExactlyOne, callSummary). No finding's disposition in this run rests on them, so no Law-1 exposure follows. Independently noted: the Tier-3 discovery that the PRE-EXISTING invariant harness had gone vacuous (59 of 60 claims reverting and being swallowed by the handler's catch, invariants passing on empty state) is a genuine and important catch that invalidated the prior run's Tier-3 result and is exactly the vacuous-invariant-harness failure mode on record.

whyNoHighOrMediumAudit.adversarialCrossCheckAudit: CONCUR. I independently searched for a non-owner-triggered harm path and found none new this run. Attacker-facing value questions on the claim payment path (zero-payment floor, first-claimer discount capture) are already carried as pre-existing ledger L-01 and QA-01 and are not re-litigated here. The PARK-001 window-reset griefing is correctly capped: strictly negative-EV, the griefer's own batchMint take shrinks by exactly what they delay, no competitor is excluded, no value is destroyed or redirected.
whyNoHighOrMediumAudit.noMediumRuling: REJECTED. See L-01 and L-02 above. The noMedium statement asserts that 'every value item was tested for permanence and none survived' — but the permanence test for L-02 was left explicitly unresolved and flagged for human review, and the evidence that resolves it against the classifier's reading sits in the same sibling repo the classifier had already mined for SWING-001. A noMedium ruling cannot rest on a swing factor the same document declares open.

M-02 (run-14) = CLASS-004 / DEDUP-005 — documented sink retirement permanently destroys the streamer buffer (value leak)

CLASS-004 needs one — extend test/NudgeStreamerLiveness_SYA.t.sol: fund a (oldSink, USDC) buffer, repoint via setNudgeAddress, then pause / de-whitelist / zero-streamer the old sink and assert no address can recover the buffer.
